name: What needs to be done before repairing water-damaged drywall in a bathroom?

mainEntity.name: What needs to be done before repairing water-damaged drywall in a bathroom?

acceptedAnswer.text: Before a contractor begins patching or hanging new drywall, the source of moisture must be completely identified and resolved. Whether caused by an active plumbing leak, leaking fixture, failing grout, or improper ventilation, closing up a wet wall cavity only hides ongoing damage. Homeowners should clear the bathroom vanity and nearby cabinets, ensure water supplies can be accessed if a pipe repair is required, and allow the interior framing to dry thoroughly. Once the plumbing leak is fixed and framing studs are dry, the contractor can cut clean borders around the damaged area and install sound backing.
acceptedAnswer.description: Fix the moisture or plumbing leak first and let the wall cavity dry completely. Patching over damp framing traps moisture and ruins the new drywall repair.
